subject: English
topic: Sentence Completion — Fill in the Blanks

questions.stem: Despite her ______ schedule, she found time to volunteer at the local shelter every weekend.

options.option_text: relaxed (relaxed schedule contradicts finding it difficult to find time)
hectic (correct: hectic = full of activity/busy; despite a busy schedule, she volunteered ✓)
flexible (flexible schedule would make it easy to volunteer — no contrast with 'despite')
boring (boring schedule doesn't logically contrast with volunteering)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Despite' signals a contrast — the blank must be a word that creates a difficulty. 'Hectic' (frantic, extremely busy) creates the contrast: despite being very busy, she still found time. 'Relaxed' and 'flexible' would make it easy to volunteer, removing the contrast. Vocabulary: hectic = full of unceasing activity.

questions.stem: The scientist's ______ research over two decades finally resulted in a groundbreaking discovery.

options.option_text: hasty (hasty = done too quickly without enough care — contradicts 'two decades' of effort)
diligent (correct: diligent = showing steady, careful effort over time; two decades of diligent research ✓)
careless (careless research over two decades contradicts a groundbreaking discovery)
sporadic (sporadic = occurring at irregular intervals; contradicts sustained effort over decades)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Diligent' = showing careful and persistent effort. Two decades of steady work leading to a breakthrough = diligent research. 'Hasty' (quick/careless) and 'sporadic' (irregular) contradict the sustained two-decade timeline. 'Careless' contradicts the positive outcome. Vocabulary: diligent = industrious, painstaking, assiduous.

questions.stem: The new regulation was ______ by all stakeholders, leading to its smooth implementation.

options.option_text: rejected (rejected contradicts 'smooth implementation')
opposed (opposed by all stakeholders would have hindered implementation)
welcomed (correct: welcomed = received gladly; welcomed by all → smooth implementation ✓)
ignored (ignored by stakeholders would not lead to smooth implementation)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Smooth implementation' is a positive outcome that requires stakeholder support. 'Welcomed' (received enthusiastically) by all stakeholders logically leads to smooth implementation. All other options (rejected, opposed, ignored) would impede implementation, not enable it.

questions.stem: The judge's verdict was considered ______ by many observers, as it seemed to favour one party without adequate justification.

options.option_text: impartial (impartial = treating all parties equally; contradicts 'seemed to favour one party')
biased (correct: biased = unfairly preferring one party; matches 'seemed to favour one party without justification' ✓)
prudent (prudent = wise and careful; doesn't match unjustified favouritism)
commendable (commendable = deserving praise; contradicts the criticism implied)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Biased' = unfairly favouring one side without adequate reason. The sentence says the verdict 'seemed to favour one party without adequate justification' — this is the definition of bias. 'Impartial' is the opposite. 'Prudent' and 'commendable' are positive words that contradict the critical tone.

questions.stem: The government's decision to ______ subsidies on essential commodities was appreciated by the common people.

options.option_text: withdraw (withdraw subsidies = remove subsidies; not appreciated by common people)
increase (correct: increasing subsidies on essential commodities would be appreciated by common people ✓)
abolish (abolish = eliminate completely; not appreciated by common people)
curtail (curtail = reduce; not appreciated by common people)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The sentence says the decision was 'appreciated' — a positive response from common people. Subsidies help common people; increasing them would be welcomed. 'Withdraw', 'abolish', and 'curtail' all mean reducing/removing subsidies, which would not be appreciated.

questions.stem: The child's ______ nature made him popular among teachers and peers alike; he was always eager to help.

options.option_text: aggressive (aggressive nature would NOT make a child popular for being 'eager to help')
selfish (selfish nature contradicts 'always eager to help')
benign (benign = gentle and kind; benign + eager to help + popular ✓)
arrogant (arrogant nature contradicts being popular and helpful)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Benign' = gentle, kindly, not harmful. A benign child who is eager to help would naturally be popular with teachers and peers. 'Aggressive', 'selfish', and 'arrogant' all contradict the helping behaviour and popularity described. Vocabulary: benign = kindly, gentle; opposite = malignant (in medical context) or malevolent.

questions.stem: Her speech was so ______ that the audience could not understand a single point she was trying to make.

options.option_text: lucid (lucid = clear and easy to understand; contradicts audience not understanding)
coherent (coherent = logical and consistent; would aid understanding)
convoluted (correct: convoluted = extremely complex and difficult to follow; audience could not understand ✓)
articulate (articulate = expressing ideas clearly; would aid understanding)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Convoluted' = unnecessarily complex; difficult to follow. A convoluted speech would explain why the audience could not understand. 'Lucid', 'coherent', and 'articulate' are all positive words meaning clear communication — they contradict the audience's inability to understand.

questions.stem: The ______ of the new CEO transformed the struggling company into a market leader within five years.

options.option_text: incompetence (incompetence would worsen a struggling company, not make it a market leader)
acumen (correct: acumen = sharp ability to make quick, clear judgements; business acumen transformed the company ✓)
indolence (indolence = laziness; contradicts transforming a company)
negligence (negligence = careless failure to act; contradicts positive transformation)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Acumen' = the ability to make good judgements and quick decisions (often used as 'business acumen'). A CEO's acumen transforming a company is a natural positive outcome. All other options (incompetence, indolence, negligence) are negative qualities that would prevent, not enable, such transformation.

questions.stem: The forest ______ rapidly after the forest department launched an aggressive plantation drive.

options.option_text: depleted (depleted = reduced; contradicts plantation drive success)
dwindled (dwindled = became smaller; contradicts plantation growth)
regenerated (correct: regenerated = restored to life/vigour after being damaged; plantation drive → forest regenerated ✓)
deteriorated (deteriorated = became worse; contradicts plantation drive success)

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Regenerated' = grew back or was restored. A plantation drive plants trees, so the forest would regenerate (grow back). 'Depleted', 'dwindled', and 'deteriorated' all mean becoming less/worse — contradicting the positive intent and success of a plantation drive.

questions.stem: His ______ behaviour at the formal dinner embarrassed his family; he spoke loudly and interrupted others repeatedly.

options.option_text: decorous (decorous = in keeping with good taste and propriety; would NOT embarrass his family)
boisterous (correct: boisterous = noisy, energetic, and lacking restraint; matches speaking loudly and interrupting ✓)
dignified (dignified = serious and formal; contradicts the disruptive behaviour described)
courteous (courteous = polite and respectful; contradicts interrupting others)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Boisterous' = noisy, lively, and lacking restraint. The description (speaking loudly, interrupting) at a formal event matches boisterous behaviour. A formal dinner requires restraint; boisterous behaviour would embarrass the family. Antonyms: decorous, dignified, courteous, restrained — all wrong options here.
